key_insight: The study proposes a single Neural Health Index (NHI) that summarizes resting-brain energy organization into one modality-invariant score to distinguish healthy from clinical brain states.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, NHI could help stratify patients and monitor treatment response across neurological, psychiatric, neurodevelopmental, and neurodegenerative conditions using EEG, MEG, or fMRI.
method: Derived NHI from signal-based energy distributions in resting brain data.
Looked for five health-associated properties: lognormality, balanced spatial allocation, regional independence, low variance, and temporal stability.
Compared NHI across scalp/intracranial EEG, MEG, and fMRI datasets.
evidence_signal: In 808 participants, NHI reportedly separated healthy from clinical groups with >95% sensitivity and specificity in internal and external validation, and it tracked disease severity and pharmacological exposure.
watch_item: Although promising, the index needs broader prospective validation and careful standardization across acquisition sites, modalities, and patient populations before routine use.
paper_title: A Modality-Invariant Measure of Neural Health
